methods.text: Write three titles for the work before starting it.
Start with the part you understand least.
Hand the work over in silence and note where the eyes go first.
Log every choice in one line with its reason.
Measure the current version before changing anything.
Finish a working version in half the time, then spend the rest fixing it.
Turn the work upside down and mark whatever now looks wrong.
Remove the surroundings and check the work still holds up alone.

constraints.text: Works fully with scripts turned off.
Every interactive element shows a visible focus outline.

tasks.text: Inline edit in hot wax: a line of text softens into a field when clicked and sets hard again when left.
Code input in dominoes: each digit drops into its box and tips the next box ready for the one after.
Signature pad in wet ink: a mark drawn by hand bleeds and dries, and one wipe lifts it away to start again.
Timeline in tree rings: a few dated moments grow outward as rings, and today is the newest, softest edge.
Time picker in shadow: an hour and a minute are set by moving the light until the shadow falls on them.
Level meter in boiling water: bubbles rise faster as the sound gets louder and settle as it fades.

guests.text: historical | Gregor Mendel | Count the results of many small trials before naming a pattern. | died 1884
creature | Sphinx | Set a riddle at the entrance and let only clear answers through. | Greek myth

temperaments.text: Splits every question into smaller ones first.
Asks who will have to live with the result.
Agrees with the goal, argues only about the steps.
Reads back the notes before anyone leaves.

guests: historical | Leonardo da Vinci | Sketch the subject many times before deciding anything. | died 1519
historical | Benjamin Franklin | List the pros and cons, weigh them, and cross out equals. | died 1790
temperaments: Speaks rarely, and only in short verdicts.
Gets louder the more sure they are.
Concedes small points to win the big one.
Asks for a demonstration before any opinion.
methods: Show it to someone at 10 percent done.
Design for the slowest device and connection first.
Count words, clicks, and seconds, then reduce each.
Find what the audience already does and build on it.
Interview someone who dislikes the category.
Collect references, then put them away and work from memory.
constraints: Usable with one thumb on a phone.
tasks: Toggle in risograph: two ink layers slip out of register as it flips, then lock back into one clean print.
Slider in sediment: each step lays down a stratum, and dragging back scrapes the layers away.
Button in letterpress: the press bites into paper, and the deboss stays as proof it was pressed.
Loader in phosphor: a trace writes the wait across a dark screen, and the glow fades behind the beam.
Tooltip in frost: a hint crystallizes where the hand pauses and melts when it moves on.
Tabs in folded paper: panels crease and refold so the one in front always lies flat.
